title: Delta definition and interpretation
claim: Delta measures the rate of change of an option price relative to changes in the underlying asset price; mathematically the first derivative.
support: Mathematical definition and graph showing delta curve.
mechanism: Delta approximates linear sensitivity; used to estimate hedge ratios.
failure_modes: delta changes with spot and time (gamma effect)
validation: Verify delta calculations match Black-Scholes formula.

title: Gamma definition and risk implications
claim: Gamma measures the rate of change of delta; the second derivative of option value with respect to spot price.
support: Detailed explanation with delta surfaces and gamma impact on P&L.
mechanism: Large gamma creates non-linear exposure; delta-hedged positions can blow up in large moves.
failure_modes: gamma is highest near ATM and near expiration
gamma amplifies losses in gapped markets
validation: Compare gamma-predicted convexity to empirical results.

title: Vega definition and volatility sensitivity
claim: Vega measures sensitivity of option price to changes in implied volatility.
support: Definition with numerical examples showing vega changes across strike and time.
mechanism: Option price increases with volatility; vega captures that sensitivity.
failure_modes: volatility surface is not flat; skew and smile effects exist
vega changes with spot, time, and vol itself
validation: Compare vega hedges to realized vol path P&L.

title: Theta definition and time decay
claim: Theta measures change in option value due to passage of time; time decay erodes option value as expiration approaches.
support: Mathematical derivation and graphical representation of theta.
mechanism: Extrinsic value decays predictably; theta is largest for ATM options.
validation: Backtest theta decay models.

title: Rho definition and interest rate sensitivity
claim: Rho measures sensitivity of option value to changes in risk-free interest rate.
support: Derivation showing rho relationship to time-to-expiration and strike.
mechanism: Interest rates affect present value of strike and cost of carry.
failure_modes: rho is small for short-dated options
dividend yield offsets interest rate effect
validation: Test rho impact on long-dated options.

title: Call-put parity relationship
claim: For European options on non-dividend-paying stocks: call - put = stock - strike * discount_factor.
support: Derivation via replication argument and numerical examples.
mechanism: Arbitrage-free pricing requires this relationship.
validation: Scan market data for arbitrage violations.

title: Dividend effects on option pricing and exercise
claim: Dividends reduce call value and increase put value; American calls may be early-exercised just before ex-date.
support: Derivation of dividend-adjusted Black-Scholes with numerical examples.
mechanism: Dividends create carry component; call holders miss dividends if not exercised.
validation: Reconcile dividend-adjusted Greeks to market prices.

title: Black-Scholes model assumptions and limitations
claim: Black-Scholes assumes constant volatility, no transaction costs, log-normal distribution. These assumptions are frequently violated in practice.
support: Detailed review of each assumption with real-world violations.
mechanism: Violations lead to model mispricing.
failure_modes: volatility smile/skew observed in all markets
validation: Backtest strategies using alternative models.

title: Implied volatility and volatility surface
claim: Implied volatility varies by strike (skew) and expiration (term structure); IV surface is not flat.
support: Empirical evidence of volatility smile/skew across equities.
mechanism: Market prices reflect volatility expectations and risk premiums.
assumptions: Black-Scholes model used as interpolation tool
failure_modes: skew and smile dynamics vary by regime
validation: Backtest across different volatility regimes.

title: Delta hedging as continuous rebalancing
claim: Delta hedging maintains delta-neutral position by rebalancing; in continuous time, delta hedging can be arbitrarily accurate.
support: Derivation of delta-neutral portfolio; analysis of discrete rebalancing.
mechanism: Gamma P&L is offset by theta decay in continuous time.
failure_modes: spot moves faster than rehedge can execute
validation: Backtest delta hedges; compare predicted vs realized P&L.

title: Gamma scalping as profitable dynamic hedging
claim: Gamma scalping harvests profit from gamma by repeatedly buying low and selling high in delta-neutral rebalancing.
support: Explanation of gamma P&L in discrete rebalancing with worked examples.
mechanism: High-vol regimes trigger frequent rebalancing; small profits lock in.
failure_modes: transaction costs exceed gamma profits in low-vol
sharp moves can incur losses before rebalancing
validation: Compare backtest gamma P&L to realized volatility.

title: Calendar spreads and theta harvesting
claim: Long calendar spreads collect theta decay; profit if front-month IV contracts or spot remains near strike.
support: Detailed explanation of calendar spread P&L components with examples.
mechanism: Front-month theta > back-month theta; front expires first.
failure_modes: large spot moves create gamma losses
validation: Measure theta vs P&L drift; identify profitable regimes.

title: Volatility skew and its causes
claim: Out-of-the-money puts trade at higher IV than ATM (skew); post-1987 markets price jump risk and demand for downside protection.
support: Historical analysis of VIX spikes and put skew changes.
mechanism: Investors demand downside protection; puts overpriced; volatility surface slopes down.
failure_modes: skew magnitude changes with market regime
post-2008 central bank intervention altered tail hedging
validation: Backtest skew-based strategies across market cycles.

title: Correlation trading and multi-leg strategies
claim: Spread strategies exploit correlations between Greeks; require model of Greeks co-movements.
support: Examples of ratio spreads, vertical spreads, iron condors; P&L analysis.
mechanism: Different Greeks dominate at different spots; spreads tailor exposure.
failure_modes: Greeks correlated in crisis; diversification fails
validation: Measure Greeks co-movement in stress events.

title: Dividend timing and early-exercise boundaries
claim: American call on dividend-paying stock has early-exercise boundary that moves near ex-date; optimal to exercise if dividend > time value.
support: Derivation of early-exercise condition with numerical algorithm.
mechanism: Exercise captures dividend; forgone time value acceptable if dividend > time value.
validation: Reconcile exercise boundaries to actual assignments.

title: P&L decomposition: Greeks attribution
claim: Option P&L can be decomposed into theta, gamma, vega, rho, residual.
support: Mathematical decomposition using Taylor expansion with worked examples.
mechanism: P&L = theta*dt + gamma*dS^2 + vega*dIV + rho*dr + residual.
validation: Compare predicted P&L to actual realized.

title: Vega hedging and volatility exposure management
claim: Vega hedging reduces IV sensitivity; vega hedges using options cheaper than delta hedges but introduce gamma exposure.
support: Explanation of vega hedge mechanics; cost comparison.
mechanism: Different strikes have different Vegas; combining creates vega-neutral.
validation: Compare vega hedge to delta hedging performance.

title: Risk limits and Greeks-based monitoring
claim: Risk managers use Greeks-based limits to monitor and control portfolio risk.
support: Examples of risk limit frameworks and Greeks-based alerts.
mechanism: Greeks aggregation provides portfolio sensitivity snapshot.
validation: Verify limits catch extreme moves.

title: Execution algorithms and market impact
claim: Large option trades incur market impact; execution algorithms minimize by breaking orders across time and strikes.
support: Discussion of VWAP, TWAP, adaptive algorithms; impact measurement.
mechanism: Demand pressure moves prices; splitting orders reduces shock.
assumptions: market impact linear in order size
validation: Backtest execution algorithms; measure impact.

title: Regulatory constraints on options trading
claim: Position limits, margin requirements, and reporting rules vary by exchange and jurisdiction.
support: Overview of position limits and margin rules as of 2012.
mechanism: Regulators impose limits to prevent systemic risk.
validation: Reconcile backtests to real limits.

title: Greeks interdependencies and portfolio effects
claim: Greeks are interdependent; portfolio Greeks aggregation requires careful handling of covariances.
support: Inferred from chapters 10-12.
mechanism: Greeks capture different dimensions of risk.
validation: Test portfolio Greeks aggregation.

title: Market microstructure impact on Greeks arbitrage
claim: Greeks arbitrage opportunities depend critically on market microstructure; opportunities vary across venues and times.
support: Inferred from chapters 5, 6, 11, 13.
mechanism: Arbitrage edges depend on transaction costs.
validation: Verify Greeks arbitrage persistence across time.

title: Data quality and model robustness requirements
claim: Greeks depend on high-quality market data; gaps create model robustness risks.
support: Inferred from chapters 9, 11, 13.
mechanism: Data errors propagate to Greeks and P&L.
validation: Reconcile backtest Greeks to market Greeks.
